about.title: Tracy Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Tracy happens because someone else was careless — on I-205 during the Friday afternoon rush, along Grant Line Road, at a job site, or in a care facility — the family is left carrying grief and paperwork at the same time. A wrongful death claim is the civil path California gives survivors. It runs separately from any criminal case the San Joaquin County District Attorney may bring, and it does not depend on a conviction. Who can file is limited: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs if none of those exist. The claim can seek funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. The clock matters. California generally allows two years from the date of death, and far less when a public entity is involved. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on I-205 near Tracy. Is a wrongful death claim different from the police investigation?
items.answer: Yes. The police report and any charges the District Attorney pursues belong to the criminal process, which is handled by the government. A wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings, and it can move forward whether or not anyone is charged or convicted. The two cases use different standards of proof and serve different purposes.

items.question: How long do we have to act in California?
items.answer: The general rule is two years from the date of death. If a public entity such as a city, county or state agency might be responsible, a formal claim usually has to be presented much sooner, often within months. Because that shorter path is easy to miss, it helps to speak with an attorney early even if your family is not ready to make decisions.

items.question: Does it cost anything to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our team handles wrongful death cases on contingency. That means no attorney fee is owed unless there is a recovery. You can ask questions first and decide later.
